children.name: Graneledone verrucosa
children.description: Graneledone verrucosa is a species of octopus in the family Megaleledonidae. The species is native to the North Atlantic Ocean.

children.name: Pareledone felix Allcock, Strugnell, Prodohl, Piatkowski & Vecchione, 2007
Pareledone turqueti
children.description: Turquet's octopus is a species of benthic octopus with a circumpolar Antarctic distribution. The species has a wide depth range, occurring from shallow waters to 4,000 m deep.

children.name: Megaleledone setebos
children.description: Megaleledone setebos, the giant Antarctic octopus, is a very large venomous octopus with a circum-Antarctic distribution. It grows to at least 28 cm in mantle length and 90 cm in total length. setebos feeds by drilling small holes in large, shelled mollusks, and then injecting its toxic saliva.

children.name: Adelieledone piatkowski Allcock, Hochberg, Rodhouse & Thorpe, 2003
Adelieledone polymorpha
children.description: Adelieledone polymorpha, or the Antarctic knobbed octopus, is a species of octopus found in the Antarctic. It was first described by Guy Coburn Robson in 1930, based on specimens found in South Georgia.
